topIssues.title: kona-sp1-proposer: detect a second instance running with the same key
topIssues.author: digorithm
topIssues.body:
The proposer assumes it is the only instance running with its key. If two run at once (most commonly a Kubernetes rolling update overlapping old and new pods, a local debug run against a live network, or two deployments sharing a remote signer key), nothing unsafe happens: the factory's UUID dedup rejects duplicate games. But the two instances race nonces, spam reverted transactions, and can create redundant sibling games that each cost a bond. It is a silent gas leak that looks like flaky infrastructure.

The proposer can detect this itself. If it discovers an on-chain game created by its own address that it did not create in this process (created after startup, not tracked by the creation guard), the only explanation is another instance with the same key. On detection: log an error, bump a dedicated metric, and optionally pause creation. Small change, fits naturally into the sync loop's game classification.

Prevention on the ops side, independent of this change: use `strategy: Recreate` (or a single-replica StatefulSet) so deploys never overlap two pods, keep the proposer key in exactly one workload's secret, and alert on sustained game-creation or nonce errors.

Related: #22019 (sync_games decomposition) touches the same code; these could land together.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: port op-succinct fault-proof proposer (create path)
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Ports succinctlabs/op-succinct's fault-proof proposer (`fault-proof` crate @ [`13716c2c`](https://github.com/succinctlabs/op-succinct/tree/13716c2ca316babb41d92369bd7bb0312611ed5f/fault-proof)) into `rust/kona/sp1/crates/proposer` as `kona-sp1-proposer`: the Rust proposer for the super-root `ZKDisputeGame` (game type 10). PR 1 of two: **create path** (game creation, resolution, two-phase bond claiming). The **defend path** (challenge detection, proof requests, `prove()`) follows under #21463.

Part of #21414 (create path; #21414 stays open until the prove() interaction lands in PR 2, #21463). Supersedes #21995 (the Go op-proposer adaptation): `op-proposer/` is untouched here and gets deprecated after the ZK upgrade, per team decision that one Rust application should own propose+prove. The proposer-agnostic pieces of #21995 (`gameargs.ParseZK`, `ZKGameImpl` parser cutover, `WaitForZKGameCount` DSL) are salvaged into this PR.

### Port fidelity

The runtime skeleton (pinned-L1 sync discipline, game DAG + canonical head selection, task scheduler, backup, cursor walk) is a **near-verbatim port** - 90-100% line-identical after mechanical renames - so upstream fixes to that machinery can be cross-applied by diff. Adaptation is confined to the contract/data-source seams:

- **Claims from the supernode**: `superroot_atTimestamp` supplies the super-root proof preimage, root claim (`keccak256(proof)`), and safe/finalized timestamp views gating cadence (`PROPOSAL_SAFETY=safe|finalized`). `SuperRootAtTimestampResponse` in `super-range-executor` gains the safe/finalized fields the Go server already serves.
- **extraData** = `parentIndex (4B BE) || superRootProof`; UUID-collision handling advances the timestamp (fresh proof fetch each step), bounded by the safety limit.
- **Discovered-game validation** against the canonical super root; a timestamp that is not yet safe locally is *pending* (excluded from parent selection, re-validated each sync, persisted across restarts) rather than terminally dropped - this also structurally prevents the far-future-parent liveness stall flagged in #21995's security review.
- **Catch-up cadence**: a head lagging by more than one interval proposes at the newest proposable timestamp instead of crawling across the gap (restart after downtime, devstack time warps).
- **Identity**: op-succinct's aggregationVkey/rangeVkeyCommitment/rollupConfigHash triplet collapses to `absolutePrestate()` (the super-aggregation program vkey, `PROGRAM_VKEY` env) + `verifier()`.
- **Two-phase DelayedWETH claiming**: unlock once finalized, payout once the withdrawal delay elapses **in L1 time** (chain time, not wall time - they diverge under devstack time travel).
- **Not ported** (deliberate): `challenger.rs` (op-challenger owns challenge/close, #21983), `prover.rs` + all proving config (PR 2), sp1-cluster + GCP KMS dependencies, alt-DA features, the anvil test harness (devstack supersedes it).

### Devstack / acceptance

The ZK preset now starts the real proposer (first env-configured sysgo service; `LOG_FORMAT=json` so the readiness matcher can parse the startup line) unless `SkipHonestProposer`. The four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests keep manual control via `WithoutHonestProposer()`. One CI change: the `RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_SP1_PROPOSER` export (the workspace build already produces and persists the binary).

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p kona-sp1-proposer --lib`: 21 tests (canonical-head DAG selection incl. catch-up chains, proposal timing incl. catch-up rule, bounded collision walk, pending-game parent ineligibility, two-phase claim state machine + chain-time maturity, backup schema guard, GameStatus/ProposalStatus enum pins vs Types.sol, 140-byte gameArgs decode with the same vectors as Go's gameargs tests, extraData encoding with #21995's vectors).
- Acceptance (verified locally, real binary + contracts + supernode, all PASS): `TestProposerCreatesRootZKGame`, `TestProposerChainsSecondZKGameOnFirst`, `TestProposerResolvesOwnUnchallengedGame`, `TestProposerClaimsBondAfterResolution` (full unlock -> delay -> payout cycle).
- Regression: the four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests pass; `just lint-go` clean; clippy/fmt clean; `git diff -- op-proposer/` is empty; `op-e2e/system/proofs` (Go proposer) passes.
- In a long local run the binary chained 51 games (root at parentIndex uint32.max, then 0 -> 1 -> ... -> 50) and self-resolved 49 of them.

## Notes for reviewers

- Textual overlap with #21983 (challenger) in `multichain_proofs.go` and the ZK acceptance setup; whichever lands second rebases. The merged ZK devstack branch should start both the challenger and this proposer.
- `ZKDisputeGame.sol` was derived from the older op-succinct commit `c13844a9`; this port tracks `13716c2c`.
- Plan: `.claude/plans/2026-07-24-feat-kona-sp1-proposer-port-plan.md` (local).

topPRs.title: contracts: revive SuperchainTokenBridge + add SuperchainERC20Factory (wrap/unwrap)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
# Description

This PR revives the `SuperchainTokenBridge` and adds a new `SuperchainERC20Factory` that lets any existing ERC20 be wrapped into a `SuperchainERC20` and moved across the Superchain.

## Commit 1: revive the SuperchainTokenBridge

`SuperchainTokenBridge`, `SuperchainERC20`, and `IERC7802` were removed in #19999 (and #20141) as unused interop contracts. This commit restores them from history at their original semvers and predeploy slot (`0x4200...0028`), adapted to the predeploy machinery that has landed since (`Predeploys.getAllRecords()` registry, `L2ContractsManager` deploy/upgrade flow, gate assertions in `L2Genesis`). The bridge is gated behind interop exactly like `SuperchainETHBridge`/`ETHLiquidity`. The legacy `OptimismSuperchainERC20` lane (beacon, factory, `L2StandardBridgeInterop`) is intentionally not revived; the new factory below replaces it.

## Commit 2: SuperchainERC20Factory

A minimal wrap/unwrap factory, added as an interop-gated predeploy at `0x4200...0026` (the slot freed by the old `OptimismSuperchainERC20Factory`):

- `deploy(chainId, token, name, symbol, decimals)` deploys a `SuperchainWrappedERC20` via CREATE2 with `salt = keccak256(chainId, token)`. The wrapped token's constructor takes no arguments (metadata is read back from the factory during construction), so its initcode is constant and **the wrapped token address is identical on every chain**, derived purely from the `[chain_id, address]` identity of the original token.
- On the original token's chain, metadata is read from the token itself (falling back to caller-supplied values for tokens without the metadata extension). On remote chains the deployer supplies it — or, better, uses propagation:
- `propagate(token, toChainId)` sends the canonical wrapped metadata from the token's home chain to the factory on another chain via the `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` (the factory is the same predeploy address everywhere, mirroring `SuperchainTokenBridge.sendERC20`/`relayERC20`). `relayDeploy` on the destination requires the messenger, the factory itself as cross-domain sender, and **message source chain == the token's claimed home chain**, so remote chains get authentic metadata without trusting any caller.
- `wrap(token, amount)` escrows original tokens in the factory and mints the wrapped token 1:1 (mints the actually-received amount, so fee-on-transfer tokens can't inflate supply beyond backing). Only possible on the token's home chain.
- `unwrap(token, amount)` burns wrapped tokens and releases escrow.
- The wrapped token is a standard `SuperchainERC20`: `crosschainMint`/`crosschainBurn` are gated to the `SuperchainTokenBridge`, so once deployed on two chains, `sendERC20`/`relayERC20` move it between them. Escrow on the home chain always equals global wrapped supply.

## Notes for reviewers

- The revive commit restores the bridge byte-for-byte where possible; the only source adaptations are the solady import path (the versioned `@solady-v0.0.245` remapping no longer exists; the vendored solady is v0.0.158) and registration in the new predeploy registry.
- `L2ContractsManager` semver bumped 1.13.0 → 1.14.0.
- Rebasing tokens are not supported by the wrap/unwrap escrow (negative rebases can strand late unwrappers), same caveat as any escrow wrapper.

## Tests

- Restored `SuperchainTokenBridge` and `SuperchainERC20` unit tests.
- New suites for the factory (deterministic addresses, home/remote metadata, propagate/relayDeploy auth + source-chain checks, wrap/unwrap, fee-on-transfer, escrow accounting) and the wrapped token (factory/bridge mint-burn gating, ERC7802 interface).

topPRs.title: op-reth: forward eth_getBlockReceipts to historical endpoint
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784709825702899)_

**Before:** `eth_getBlockReceipts` and several other block-parameterized read methods (`eth_getHeaderByNumber`/`ByHash`, `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber`/`ByHash`, `eth_getUncleCountByBlockNumber`/`ByBlockHash`, `eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`, `eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`, `eth_getRawTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`) for pre-bedrock blocks were served locally by op-reth, which has no pre-bedrock data, instead of being forwarded to the configured historical RPC endpoint like the other block-based methods.

**After:** `eth_getBlockReceipts` and all of the above block-parameterized methods for a pre-bedrock block are forwarded to the historical endpoint, matching `eth_getBlockByNumber`/`eth_getBlockByHash` and the rest of the forwarded set.

Since plain l2geth does not implement `eth_getBlockReceipts`, the middleware additionally stitches the response when the forwarded call comes back with JSON-RPC error `-32601` (method not found): it fetches the block from the historical endpoint with transaction hashes only (`full=false`) and issues one `eth_getTransactionReceipt` per hash (pre-bedrock OP Mainnet blocks contain exactly one transaction), returning the legacy receipt objects verbatim — self-consistent with what the forwarded `eth_getTransactionReceipt` already returns. Historical endpoints that serve `eth_getBlockReceipts` natively (op-erigon, routing proxies) keep the single-call forward path.

Edge cases: a block unknown to the historical endpoint returns `null` (mirroring a node that serves the method natively), a block without transactions returns `[]`, and any failure while stitching returns a JSON-RPC error to the caller instead of falling through to local handling (which cannot serve pre-bedrock receipts). All other forwarded methods keep the existing behavior exactly.

**How:** In `rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/historical.rs`: added the methods to the position-0 block-id arm of `extract_block_id_for_method`, and added a `-32601`-triggered stitch path (`stitch_block_receipts` / `fetch_stitched_block_receipts`) to `HistoricalRpcInner::forward_to_historical`. Unit tests cover block-id extraction plus mocked-transport tests for the native forward path, the stitch path (number and hash params), empty block, unknown block, receipt-failure error, and fall-through preservation for other methods.

Fixes #21031

topPRs.title: interopsmoke: add chained-invalid-message smoke test
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
> Stacked on #22074 — review/merge that first; this PR targets its branch.

## Description

Adds a smoke test verifying that interop invalidation is **transitive**.

Chain A sends a cross-domain message targeting an `EventLogger` on chain B. Chain B relays it with a corrupted identifier, so the relay is invalid. The relay still executes and calls `emitLog`, emitting a new initiating message that exists *only because the invalid relay ran*. Chain A then executes that message. When chain B's block is replaced, chain A's executing message must be reorged out too.

Two independent dependent arms are asserted:
1. A message depending on the invalid block itself.
2. A plain log emitted on a *later* chain B block, executed on chain A — that block is valid in itself and is replaced only because its ancestor is. This covers invalidation through the block lineage, which a node could otherwise miss while still correctly invalidating direct dependencies.

A control message that does not depend on the invalid block is asserted to survive, so a node that discards a swathe of recent chain A blocks does not pass.


## Tests

New smoke test in `op-chain-ops/interopsmoke`. `go build ./...` passes.

topPRs.title: ci: cache final rust-workspace-binaries outputs
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C09E7EJGN5P/p1784158570945069)_

Follow-up to #21832 (now merged), split out per review.

**Before:** `rust-workspace-binaries` rebuilds the full release workspace (~13.5 min) on every pipeline, gating `go-tests-short`/`go-tests-full` and the sysgo acceptance jobs — so Go-only PRs wait ~14 min for unchanged binaries, while `rust-build-op-rbuilder` skips its build in 33s via its final-binary cache.

**After:** when the `rust/` tree, the mise toolchain pins, and the superchain-registry submodule pin are unchanged, the three workspace binaries (`kona-host`, `kona-node`, `op-reth`) are restored from cache in ~30s and the cargo build is skipped entirely.

**How:** a new reusable `rust-binary-cached-build` command in `main.yml`, wired into both `rust-workspace-binaries` invocations via `rust-build-binary`'s new `binary_cache_binaries` parameter, and into `rust-workspace-release` in rust-e2e.yml (same build parameters and consumers, so it shares the same cache key). The shell logic lives in `.circleci/scripts/rust-binary-cache.sh` with three subcommands — `compute-key` (writes the checksum inputs: sha256 of `git ls-tree -r HEAD` + the profile/features/package/binary parameters, plus the sorted binary list), `build` (hit-check, else cargo build + collect the named binaries), and `stage` (lay the binaries out for `persist_to_workspace`). Only `restore_cache`/`save_cache` remain YAML steps, as CircleCI requires. Both the hit and build paths persist exactly the named binaries at `rust/target/release/`, so downstream jobs see an identical workspace layout either way.

**Deletes the old `rust-build-vendored` job** (second commit): the job reimplemented this exact pattern inline — 134 lines, ~65 of them inline shell for the tree-hash key, hit-check, build-skip, and binary collection. `rust-build-op-rbuilder` / `rust-build-rollup-boost` now route through the same command via `rust-build-binary` (a new `extra_hash_paths` parameter covers their sibling `path`-dep closure). Net effect on this PR vs develop: **403 insertions / 178 deletions** (179 of the insertions are the script; the migration commit alone is +44/−158). Behavior deltas for the vendored builds, all intentional:

- They now restore the shared dep/toolchain caches (keyed on their own `Cargo.lock`s, which `op-rbuilder-checks`/`rollup-boost-checks` already populate), so a binary-cache miss no longer re-downloads every crate. They are restore-only (`save_cache: false`) — a single-package build must not save a partial registry under the shared key.
- Their cache key now includes the mise toolchain pins and the superchain-registry submodule pin (previously a toolchain bump did **not** invalidate the vendored binaries — a latent staleness bug), and moves from the `rust-<dir>-v9-…` namespace to `rust-workspace-bins-v1-…`, so each job rebuilds once on first run and caches thereafter.
- Binaries persist at `rust/<dir>/target/release/<bin>` — the same layout as the workspace binaries — so the `.circleci-cache/rust-binaries` special case in the sysgo consumers (`main.yml` acceptance jobs + `helpers.yml` `rust-setup-env`) is deleted too.

Job/check names are unchanged, and the workspace builds' cache key is byte-identical before and after (verified by running `compute-key` locally with the workspace parameters).

Dep-cache interplay: the command keeps the same shared dep/toolchain cache restore+save as the normal build path, so on a binary-cache miss from a rust-only change the exact-key dep cache usually hits and prepopulates the crate downloads (sccache covers recompilation, not downloads); a `Cargo.lock` change fully refreshes the dep cache per its existing no-fallback design (and also changes the binary key, landing on the build path). If the dep key was evicted while the binary key is still live, the hit path re-seeds the registry with `cargo fetch` rather than tripping #21832's empty-save guard.

---
